method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: What is the problem of the criterion? Particularism, methodism and the wheel
What are the central questions of epistemology: the nature, sources, structure and extent of knowledge?
Plato's Theaetetus: knowledge as perception, true judgement, true judgement with an account

evidence.excerpt: A popular form of the Problem of the Criterion can be raised by asking two seemingly innocent questions
there are only three responses to the Problem of the Criterion: particularism, methodism, and skepticism
we are forced to beg the question
Robert Amico (1988b) argues that Chisholm’s “solution” is clearly unacceptable
Chisholm claims that particularism is superior to methodism and skepticism because by being a particularist one can give a reasonable account of knowledge
“the problem of the criterion has no solution” (1988, 234)
It comes to us from Book 2 of Sextus Empiricus’ Outlines of Pyrrhonism
The problem resurfaced in the late 1500’s with Michael De Montaigne’s “Apology for Raymond Sebond”
In the late 19th and early 20th centuries Cardinal D.J. Mercier (1884) and his student P. Coffey (1917) again reminded the world of the problem.
Perhaps the Problem of the Criterion is rather a set of related problems.
